messages:
matt: We need a concise plan for per-org rate limiting that degrades smoothly when GPU pools saturate. My rough idea: dynamic token-bucket refill that scales with pool headroom + shedding non-critical routes.

sophia: Sounds good. Can you sketch the math? how do bursts work vs sustained load?

matt: Sure — keep it simple: compute a headroom ratio from pool utilization and scale refill by that. Pseudocode: 
```
soft_threshold = 0.75
headroom = max(0, 1 - (gpu_util - soft_threshold) / (1 - soft_threshold))
refill_per_sec = base_rate * headroom
```
This means when util <= 75% we give full refill, above that we proportionally reduce. Bursts are covered by a small per-org burst bucket (configurable).

raj: Edge cases: long-lived streaming calls can still hammer the pool even if refill is low. We should charge streams per-token produced but also count reserved KV cache and runtime slices as in-flight capacity so admission control can block new streams sooner.

tina: Also we must preserve paid tiers. Add a reserved_capacity per-pricing-tier so headroom = (pool_capacity - reserved)/pool_capacity when computing refill share. Otherwise enterprise customers get starved.

matt: Yep — reserved tiers + weighted sharing. Metrics to emit: `pool_utilization`, `effective_refill_ratio`, `org_reject_rate`, `queue_length`, `avg_latency_by_route`.

ops-bot: plan: canary in us-west on dedicated-pool-3. Monitor p95 latency and error-rate for 48h, then ramp 4x.

sophia: Fairness question: tiny orgs vs many small concurrent orgs. Proposal: weight = max(min_weight, committed_units^(0.5)) so a few active workers don't dominate. We should simulate with our request traces.

raj: Also note region-local constraints — don't aggregate headroom across regions. Refill decisions must be per-region per-pool; otherwise cross-region failover will create sudden egress/network pressure.

matt: Agreed. Next steps: I'll open a design PR with a simulator (stochastic traces) and a small staging admission controller that implements the refill formula + burst tokens. Can someone take the dashboard? @sophia?

sophia: I'll own the dashboard and alerts. Will add panels for 95/99 latency, reject-rate by org, headroom ratio, and tail queue length. Alerts: reject-rate > 0.5% sustained or p95 latency increase > 15%.

tina: Add a kill-switch in the service to revert to static per-key limiter if things go sideways. Also include a support runbook for on-call.

matt: Good. I'll include a short rollout plan in the PR: canary -> region ramp -> global after 72h without regressions. Link to design doc when it's up: https://go/redwood/infra/dynamic-refill (internal). :thumbsup:

ops-bot: noted. tagging: @eng-sre for runbook review.

sophia: One more thought: we should measure cost delta (tokens saved) from batching and refill behavior to quantify ROI. I'll add cost panels.

matt: Thanks all — will post PR link and a sim result snapshot tomorrow.
